instagram_carousel.caption:
What is a prenup in Australia? The legal term is a binding financial agreement, a contract made under Part VIIIA of the Family Law Act 1975 for married couples. It can be signed before the wedding, during the marriage or after it ends.

What makes it hold? As at November 2026, the Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia states an agreement is only binding if it meets the technical requirements of the Act, and that each of you must receive independent legal advice from an Australian lawyer before you sign.

Legal Aid NSW lists the formal requirements, including:
1. It is in writing.
2. It says which part of the Family Law Act it is made under.
3. It is signed by all parties.
4. It is made after both parties have received independent legal advice.

Victoria Legal Aid adds that both of you must have your own lawyers, and each lawyer gives a signed statement confirming the advice was provided.

Who does it tend to suit? Legal Aid NSW says an agreement can protect an inheritance a partner may receive in future, or property for children from a previous relationship. It also notes that once you make one, you usually cannot go to court later to divide property.

Marrying abroad? Legal Aid NSW says an agreement made overseas is not automatically recognised in Australia and must meet the formal requirements to be valid here.

This is general information, not legal advice, and each partner needs their own independent legal advice.
